research.abstract: Abstract Background TB vaccine development is hampered by the natural history of M. tuberculosis: most infected people rarely progress to disease, so trials must be very large and long to accrue sufficient disease endpoints. Current trials enrol IGRA-positive participants (IGRA: Interferon-Gamma Release Assays), but IGRAs remain positive for many years and cannot distinguish recent from remote infection. Tests for recent infection are now in development, and we argue they could make trials substantially more efficient. Here, we investigate how screening participants prior to enrolment with a test for recent M.tb infection could impact the total number of enrollees required for an adequately-powered TB vaccine trial. Methods Using a statistical model of vaccine trial recruitment, we estimated the number needed to contact, test, and enrol to achieve an ‘effective’ trial (defined as 50 disease endpoints), under IGRA-gated enrolment (life-long duration of positivity) vs. enrolment with a test for recent infection. We considered five recruitment strategies: non-test-based enrolment for ages 15-49, ages 12-34, and household contacts of recent cases; and test-based enrolment using IGRA, and a test for recent infection with two-year duration of positivity. The model explored trial recruitment in South Africa, Kenya, and India. Results Compared with an extended-positivity test, a test for recent infection reduced the median number needed to enrol by 4.2- to 6-fold under favourable conditions. It also outperformed non-test-based strategies, including enrolling household contacts. This comes at the cost of substantially more testing, but crude estimates suggest recency-based enrolment would still be cheaper overall provided the new test does not cost more than roughly 5-10 times an IGRA. Conclusions Diagnostics for recent M.tb infection have the potential to improve vaccine trial efficiency, but more research is now needed to understand test characteristics and to evaluate their use in this setting. Our Viewpoint sets out the test attributes that would need to be established, such as time to positivity, duration of positivity, sensitivity, and specificity, before such tests could be used in vaccine trials.

research.abstract: Introduction The WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List identifies antibiotic-resistant bacteria posing a serious health threat. We aimed to analyse age-specific and region-specific burden trajectories and inequalities across countries with different socio-development levels for these pathogens. Methods We conducted a systematic analysis (1990-2021) using the Global Burden of Disease Study's Measuring Infectious Causes and Resistance Outcomes for Burden Estimation database, assessing trends and inequalities in mortality burden attributable to priority pathogens by age and region. Analyses included age-period-cohort modelling, average annual percentage change (AAPC) and health inequality metrics across countries stratified by sociodemographic index (SDI). Results Global mortality attributable to priority antibiotic-resistant pathogens rose from 5.47 to 6.12 per 100 000 in 1990-2021 (annual net drift: 0.086%). By age, mortality declined in under 5 but increased in the middle-aged and elderly (peaking at 40-44 and ≥95), primarily driven by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella (AAPC 2.1%-2.4%) and Escherichia coli (AAPC 1.6%-2.2%). Mortality from multidrug-resistant tuberculosis rose across all ages, particularly in neonates (AAPC 7.4%, 95% CI 6.6% to 8.1%). Regionally, high-income Asia Pacific saw the steepest mortality decline (AAPC -2.5%, 95% CI -2.7% to -2.3%), while Eastern Europe exhibited the sharpest increase (AAPC 1.2%, 95% CI 0.2% to 2.2%), fueled by multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (AAPC 7.7%, 95% CI 6.0% to 9.5%), carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella (AAPC 3.5%, 95% CI 2.2% to 4.9%) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (AAPC 3.1%, 95% CI 1.5% to 4.7%). Southern sub-Saharan Africa experienced a rise in fluoroquinolone-resistant Salmonella Typhi (AAPC 4.6%, 95% CI 2.5% to 6.8%). Over the 32-year period, the slope index of inequality in mortality burden of priority pathogens narrowed from -333.65 to -282.20, while the concentration index widened from -0.28 to -0.31. Conclusions The global mortality burden of priority antibiotic-resistant pathogens increased between 1990 and 2021, with age and regional disparities demanding targeted containment. Higher burden in low-SDI regions requires equitable healthcare resource allocation to combat antimicrobial resistance.

research.abstract: Estimating the effective sample size (ESS) is fundamental in Bayesian phylogenetic inference to account for autocorrelation in MCMC samples. While methods for continuous parameters are well established, the discrete and high-dimensional nature of treespace poses substantial challenges. In this paper, we introduce a new approach based on Conditional Clade Distributions (CCDs) to emulate MCMC chains with known ESS bounds. We compare existing tree ESS estimators with novel approaches that utilize CCDs as tractable tree distributions, as well as a new probabilistic estimator based on differences in clade frequencies between independent chains. Using our emulated chains from both simulated and real datasets, we assess estimators for their ability to recover the true ESS (accuracy), their insensitivity to the removal of autocorrelated samples from the chain (stability), and their tolerance to combining multiple chains together (robustness). We further examine how multimodality and poor inter-mode chain mixing can compromise the reliability of tree ESS estimates. These findings indicate that our new CCD-based estimators perform comparably to existing approaches with respect to accuracy, stability, and robustness. In contrast, the probabilistic estimator and two previously recommended methods incur prohibitive computational costs for long chains. Together, these results establish a new framework for evaluating tree ESS estimators using CCD-based emulated MCMC chains and demonstrate their performance and current limitations in practical phylogenetic analyses. The expanded suite of tree ESS estimators is available in the user-friendly TreeStat2 software package for BEAST 2.

research.abstract: Importance: Severe maternal morbidity is increasingly driven by chronic conditions present before pregnancy, but existing obstetric comorbidity indices rely on clinician documentation and are not designed for preconception use. Objective: To determine whether conditions represented in a patient-facing preconception assessment are associated with severe maternal morbidity comparably with clinician-derived indices. Design: Retrospective cohort study of deliveries from 1992 to 2025; scores were derived from diagnoses recorded at least 280 days before delivery. Setting: Two deidentified electronic health record databases covering an academic and public health system in San Francisco and 5 other University of California medical centers. Participants: Birthing individuals aged 12 to 55 years at delivery with at least 10 clinical events recorded before conception. Exposures: Preconception Medical Assessment (PreMA) score (range, 0-8) and the Bateman (range, 0-51) and Leonard (range, 0-281) obstetric comorbidity indices, modeled per 1-SD increase. Main Outcomes and Measures: Severe maternal morbidity and nontransfusion severe maternal morbidity within 7 days of delivery, defined by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention indicators. Results: Among 58,549 deliveries (21,427 in the San Francisco cohort [mean (SD) maternal age, 33.4 (5.7) years]; 37,122 in the statewide cohort [33.1 (5.4) years]), each 1-SD increase in PreMA score was associated with severe maternal morbidity in the San Francisco cohort (relative risk [RR], 1.23; 95% CI, 1.19-1.28), similar to the Bateman (RR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.22-1.29) and Leonard (RR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.23-1.30) indices; statewide findings were consistent. Severe maternal morbidity rose from 6.6% at a score of 0 to 9.0% at 1 to 3 and 17.8% at 4 or greater (statewide, 3.8%, 5.3%, and 14.5%). Associations persisted across racial, ethnic, and neighborhood deprivation subgroups. Cardiovascular conditions (RR, 3.08; 95% CI, 2.50-3.80) and diabetes (RR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.34-2.48) were most strongly associated with nontransfusion severe maternal morbidity. Conclusions and Relevance: In this cohort study, higher scores on a patient-facing preconception assessment were associated with severe maternal morbidity, comparably with clinician-derived indices. Prospective studies are needed before scores are used clinically.

research.abstract: IncC plasmids played an important role in antimicrobial resistance development in the seventh pandemic Vibrio cholerae O1 El Tor (7PET) lineage during the 1970s and have recently begun to re-emerge. We investigated 28 complete IncC plasmids, including 17 newly sequenced genomes, from 7PET isolates collected across Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean between 1979 and 2024 and spanning the global 7PET phylogeny. Four additional IncC plasmids from other species were included, for a total of 32 IncC plasmids. IncC type 2 predominated among V. cholerae plasmids, and five novel core genome sequence types (cgSTs) were identified. Antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) occurred within diverse genetic structures inserted at specific sites in the conserved IncC backbone. Despite remarkable diversity in ARGs and associated genomic islands, the IncC backbone remained stable over five decades. These findings highlight the dynamic evolution and adaptability of IncC plasmids in 7PET under antimicrobial selection.

research.abstract: Abstract Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) has exceptionally high recurrence rates, exceeding 50%, contributing to mortality and morbidity. This recurrence rate is proposed to be due to field cancerization, a phenomenon where tumor-adjacent “field” tissue that appears histologically normal harbors molecular changes that prime it for subsequent tumor growth. Current models attribute field cancerization to shared driver mutations between tumors and adjacent at-risk tissue, but this assumption has never been directly tested. To comprehensively characterize this phenomenon, we profiled patient-matched tumor, normal-adjacent field (NAF), contralateral normal, and blood samples from HPV-negative HNSCC patients using whole genome sequencing, targeted driver gene sequencing, single-nucleus multiome profiling, spatial transcriptomics and functional proliferation assays. While histologically normal NAF tissues did harbor expanded mutant clones, these mutations rarely overlapped with paired tumors and were not shared across patients, suggesting molecular features beyond mutations are altered in NAF. Single-cell multiomics revealed that NAF epithelium loses its normal organizational hierarchy: basal stem cell markers persist in differentiated cells, while terminal differentiation programs fail to activate, with reconfiguration of both gene regulatory networks and cell-cell interactions. Proliferating cells appeared in tissue layers normally restricted to post-mitotic cells, a pattern typically seen only in overt dysplasia. Within this disrupted hierarchy, a distinct epithelial state arose in NAF that expressed both normal epithelial and tumor-associated markers, which we localized to the parabasal layers using immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomics. Together, our findings demonstrate that field cancerization operates through epithelial hierarchy disorganization that disrupts differentiation, generates cells with tumor-like features, and may create a permissive environment for the expansion of cancer-associated mutations, all within tissue that appears histologically normal.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-read sequencing has revealed complex variations, such as gene conversions in immunologically critical PE/PPE gene families, yet their role in Mycobacterium tuberculosis host adaptation remains unclear. METHODS: We performed a comparative genomic analysis across a gradient of host-imposed selective pressure: chronic within-host infection, latent household transmission, and a 21-year clonal outbreak in Bern, Switzerland. RESULTS: We observed a constrained accumulation of mutational events across distinct epidemiological settings, with rates ranging from 0.36 to 0.81 events per genome per year. Under minimal host-imposed selection, the pathogen accumulated only small-scale variants (i.e., SNPs and indels). During the outbreak, however, the genetic diversity landscape shifted toward larger-scale variants, including recurrent gene conversions and structural variations. Notably, an early PPE19-to-PPE18 conversion emerged in the ancestral strain and was maintained across the entire lineage. In contrast, 86% of variants were transient singletons, with only a small proportion persisting under selection. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest a framework in which M. tuberculosis maintains genomic stability through purifying selection, while retaining the capacity to generate adaptive diversity through large-scale genetic rearrangements in immunologically relevant genomic features under intensified host pressure.

research.abstract: Abstract Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a disease in preterm infants associated with an increased abundance of Enterobacteriaceae. FimH, a mannose-binding adhesin on Enterobacteriaceae type 1 fimbriae, mediates mucosal attachment and TLR4-dependent inflammatory cascades. We evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy of an oral FimH inhibitor (Sibofimloc) to reduce Enterobacteriaceae colonization and prevent NEC in preterm piglets. We performed a 9-d dose-escalation safety study (10, 25, 50 mg/kg BID) assessing absorption and tolerability and a 10-d randomized efficacy study. Piglets in the efficacy study received an infant formula diet with or without oral sibofimloc (40 mg/kg BID), or donor human milk (DHM) as a healthy control. NEC incidence, tissue histopathology, and gut microbiota composition via metagenomic whole-genome sequencing (WGS) were evaluated. Systemic exposure data reveal that sibofimloc was dose-dependently absorbed, while plasma levels decreased from postnatal day 2 to day 8, indicating reduced drug absorption with maturation of the intestinal barrier. Treatment with sibofimloc did not reduce NEC incidence (100% in sibofimloc in formula controls) or severity, whereas DHM-fed piglets experienced 0% NEC. Sibofimloc-treated animals exhibited significantly reduced crypt depths, demonstrating heightened mucosal injury and impaired regenerative capacity. WGS revealed that sibofimloc-treated animals maintained a gut luminal microbiota composition similar to untreated formula controls, dominated by Clostridium perfringens ( C. perfringens ). Selective targeting of FimH-expressing Enterobacteriaceae was insufficient to prevent NEC or alter the gut microbiota in this preterm piglet model, underscoring the complexity of NEC-associated microbial communities and suggesting that additional microbial targets and other colonization mechanisms may contribute to disease development.

research.abstract: Abstract Transitions to saline environments pose formidable challenges to plants, yet halophytism has evolved independently across many flowering plant lineages. We assembled a comparative angiosperm gene catalog of ∼10 million protein-coding genes from 232 genomes spanning 55 families, with similar representation of halophytes and salt-sensitive relatives, to identify convergent genomic signatures of halophytism. Halophytes show remarkable convergence with recurrent genomic trends in salt-response genes, including lower copy numbers, higher basal expression, more constrained expression variation, distinct evolutionary rates, and independent positive selection on select genes at the same amino acid sites across multiple halophyte lineages. Crops and their wild halophytic relatives differ in gene family evolution, particularly in stress-response pathways. These findings reveal repeatedly tested evolutionary routes to halophytism and establish a genomic foundation for translating convergent adaptations into salt-tolerant crops.

research.abstract: Nerve growth factor (NGF) is a neurotrophin central to sensory neuron biology and pain signaling. NGF and NTRK1 are gnathostome paralogs within the older neurotrophin and Trk families, respectively, whereas NGFR encodes p75NTR, a member of the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily. Orthology assessment of NGF, NTRK1, and NGFR across vertebrates is challenging because mature neurotrophins are short, cysteine-rich ligands, NTRK1 has closely related paralogs, and NGFR lies outside the Trk receptor family. We assessed species-level joint genomic recovery of the three genes and compared evolutionary constraint among predefined ligand and receptor regions. The analysis covered 94 chordates and combined graded recovery evidence with family phylogenies, locus and domain evidence, codon models, amino acid conservation, and structural mapping. Sixteen non-gnathostome species were included to provide evolutionary context and were not used to calculate recovery rates for the three focal genes. Among 78 sampled gnathostomes, 52 had high-confidence joint recovery, eight had supported provisional joint recovery, four had component-level evidence consistent with possible co-recovery, and 14 remained incomplete. Mature NGF had a numerically lower estimate of the ratio of nonsynonymous to synonymous substitution rates (dN/dS, ω) than the pro-domain (0.067 versus 0.352). All six scaffold cysteines were invariant; in the residue-class comparison, the cysteine scaffold was the only structural class that differed from the coordinate-resolved background after correction. The dimer-interface, TrkA-contact, and p75NTR-contact classes did not differ significantly from that background after correction. Receptor analyses yielded low ω estimates in Trk kinase domains and p75NTR intracellular regions. Together, these results provide a confidence-graded map of focal-gene recovery and regional purifying constraint while placing non-gnathostome homologs within the older neurotrophin system.

research.abstract: Abstract Small molecules that block PD-L1 bind a pocket that exists only when two PD-L1 molecules pair up, and oral compounds acting this way are in phase 2 trials. I asked whether a tumour could escape such a compound by mutating that pocket. Working from crystal structures and a codon alignment of 44 vertebrate orthologs of CD274 spanning about 429 million years, I find the drug pocket and the PD-1 binding interface are the same surface: all 10 drug-contacting residues lie within 5.0 Å of PD-1, against 1.9 expected by chance (hypergeometric p = 8.7 × 10−9), and the result holds at every distance cutoff I tested. Those residues are under purifying selection. CD274 evolves at dN /dS = 0.236, no pocket residue shows positive selection, and the pocket evolves more slowly than accessibility-matched residues elsewhere in the protein: median dN /dS = 0.077 against a permutation null median of 0.287, roughly 3.8-fold lower, p = 0.0028. That comparison stays below 0.05 across every robustness variant I ran, including every single-residue deletion. The overlap is what makes this useful: the residues a compound would have to lose are the residues PD-1 binds, so escape by pocket mutation is constrained by the very function the tumour expresses PD-L1 to perform.

research.abstract: DEG (Degradation of periplasmic proteins) proteases are ATP-independent serine endopeptidases found in bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes including plants. They are considered to be key regulators of development and stress tolerance in plants. In this study, a comprehensive genome-wide analysis identified 19 serine protease-like DEG family proteins in potato (Solanum tuberosum L.), revealing their structural diversity, domain architecture, and regulatory potential. Physiochemical profiling showed a predominance of acidic isoelectric points (pI), variable protein lengths (169–1083 amino acids), and differential stability indices. Subcellular localization predicted most DEG proteases to reside in the chloroplast, with others distributed across cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, and peroxisome. Domain analysis confirmed the universal presence of the trypsin domain, with varying numbers of PDZ domains and additional conserved motifs among paralogs. Evolutionary divergence analysis of StDEG genes and their orthologs from six Solanaceae species as well as Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, and Zea mays revealed dN/dS ratios below one for all orthologous pairs, suggesting that StDEG genes have evolved under strong purifying selection and remained highly conserved throughout plant evolution. Gene ontology annotations linked DEG proteases to key biological functions including PSII repair, photoinhibition, and chloroplast organization, alongside protein catabolism and light stimulus response. Promoter analysis revealed an abundance of cis-regulatory elements (CREs), particularly light-responsive motifs, along with hormone and stress-related elements such as ABRE, ARE, and MBS. Expression profiling across eight developmental tissues demonstrated tissue-specific expression patterns, with strong transcript accumulation of selected DEG members in senescent leaf, stolon, shoot apex, and tuber. Interestingly, several splice variants showed unique expression dynamics, including stage-specific and stress-induced activation. Upon exposure to abiotic and hormonal cues, 16 DEG proteases displayed significant transcriptional modulation, particularly under light, ABA, and Zeatin treatments, with notable fold changes reaching up to 26-fold in certain variants. These findings highlight the functional versatility of DEG proteases in potato development and stress adaptation, especially their responsiveness to light and hormonal stimuli. The characterization of these proteases paves the way for future studies on their roles in crop resilience and genome editing applications.

research.abstract: The ratio of nonsynonymous to synonymous substitutions (dN/dS) encodes important information about the selection pressures acting on protein-coding genes. In bacterial populations, dN/dS often declines with the sequence divergence between strains, but the mechanisms responsible for this broad empirical trend are still debated. Existing models have primarily focused on de novo mutations, overlooking the older genetic variants that are continually introduced through horizontal gene transfer and recombination. Here we introduce a phenomenological model of dN/dS in recombining populations of bacteria, which allows us to disentangle the effects of recombination among pairs of closely related strains. We find that clonally inherited regions of the genome exhibit consistently higher dN/dS ratios, and that the accumulation of recombined segments can quantitatively explain the majority of the decline in dN/dS. We use these observations to re-examine models of purifying selection and adaptive reversion in human gut bacteria, and uncover evidence for widespread weak selection at a large fraction of protein-coding sites. Our findings show that horizontal gene transfer can be an important factor in shaping genome-wide patterns of selective constraint, and raise new questions about the effectiveness of natural selection in complex bacterial populations.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious pathogen globally despite decades of effective chemotherapy. In 2024, an estimated 10·7 million people developed tuberculosis, including approximately 620 000 people living with HIV (PLHIV), and tuberculosis caused an estimated 1·23 million deaths overall, including approximately 150 000 deaths among PLHIV. Men accounted for more than half of the cases, and children represented a substantial burden, reflecting ongoing transmission and diagnostic gaps. Approximately a quarter of the world's population has been infected with M tuberculosis, with immunological evidence of previous or current infection. This population includes groups at increased risk of progression to tuberculosis disease, particularly those with recent infection, HIV, undernutrition, young age, or other clinical and social vulnerabilities. Following 3 years of COVID-19-related setbacks, global tuberculosis incidence declined modestly (1%) from 2023 to 2024 but remains higher than in 2020 and far off-track to meet the 2025 WHO End TB Strategy milestones. Case detection improved to 8·3 million notifications (78% of estimated incident cases), supported by expanded molecular diagnostics; however, prevalence surveys continue to reveal substantial proportions of bacteriologically confirmed but asymptomatic tuberculosis, highlighting persistent transmission and missed diagnoses. 30 high-burden countries accounted for 87% of cases, led by India, Indonesia, the Philippines, China, Pakistan, Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Bangladesh. M tuberculosis-HIV co-infection remains a major driver of mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Drug-resistant tuberculosis threatens progress: of 390 000 estimated multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis cases in 2024, only 42% initiated treatment, although treatment success improved to 71%. Tuberculosis-preventive treatment reached 5·3 million people, including 58% of PLHIV and 25% of eligible household contacts, well below global targets. Persistent undernutrition, poverty, HIV, diabetes, smoking, alcohol use, air pollution, migration, and conflict continue to shape tuberculosis epidemiology. With financing at only 27% of global targets, accelerated prevention, proactive case finding, social protection, and sustained political commitment are essential to eliminate tuberculosis.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) control in high-burden settings is complicated by the genetic diversity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), which influences transmission. This study assessed the prevalence of mixed strain infections (MSIs) and microevolutionary events, analyzing their association with biosocial and clinical variables in Fortaleza, northeastern Brazil. METHODS: This prospective study included 168 patients with pulmonary TB from two referral hospitals serving socioeconomically vulnerable populations. Mtb isolates were subjected to drug resistance testing using Xpert MTB/RIF, MGIT 960, SIRE kit, and 24-locus mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable number tandem repeat typing. Genetic diversity was classified as MSI when multiple alleles were detected at two or more loci, or as a microevolutionary event when multiple alleles were detected at a single locus. Clinical and socioeconomic data were correlated with the genotypic profiles of the patients. RESULTS: Genetic diversity was observed in 10 isolates (6%), comprising three (1.75%) MSIs and seven microevolutionary events. Among the 10 patients with genetic diversity, the median age was 46 years, and illicit drug use was reported in this subgroup. All MSIs were rifampicin-sensitive; four of the seven cases with microevolution showed rifampicin resistance. Half of the patients with genetic diversity showed poor treatment outcomes in the form of death, failure, and loss of follow-up; comorbid conditions such as diabetes, syphilis, and previous TB were common in this subgroup. CONCLUSIONS: The patterns of Mtb genetic diversity in this high-burden setting coexist with conditions of social vulnerability and complex disease presentations. These findings highlight the coexistence of Mtb genetic diversity with social and clinical vulnerability in this setting and support further investigation using larger cohorts and higher-resolution genomic approaches.

research.abstract: Abstract Enteric pathogens account for a substantial global disease burden, yet population-based surveillance remains limited by the transient nature of pathogen shedding, which constrains the sensitivity of stool-based molecular testing to a narrow detection window. Detection of IgG responses in serological surveys could enable new insights into enteric pathogen transmission, but benchmarking serological measures relative to stool-based measures of infection remains a critical evidence gap. We compared measures of disease transmission in longitudinal birth cohort samples using multiplex IgG (1,575 dried blood spots, 369 children) and PCR assays (2,229 stool samples, 369 children) that overlapped for nine pathogens (norovirus GI/GII, Shigella /enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC), Campylobacter spp., enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (LT-ETEC), Salmonella enterica , Giardia spp., Cryptosporidium spp., Entamoeba histolytica ). Campylobacter and LT-ETEC ranked highest while E. histolytica and S. enterica ranked among the lowest by both IgG and PCR measures of infection. Measures of infection were less aligned for norovirus GI, norovirus GII, Cryptosporidium , Shigella /EIEC, and Giardia . research.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly consulted for health advice, but they can produce fluent statements that are false or unsupported, known as hallucinations, and this risk is poorly characterised in low-resource languages such as Bangla. We measured hallucinations of locally deployable open-weight LLMs in Bangla diabetes question answering and tested whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounded in Bangladesh’s National Guideline on Diabetes Mellitus reduces them. Forty patient questions spanning six clinical sub-domains were each answered twice, under zero-shot prompting, by Qwen3.5-9B, TigerLLM-9B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B, and by BanglaDiaRAG, which adds hybrid dense (BGE-M3) and sparse (BM25) retrieval from a physician-reviewed Bangla guideline knowledge base to Qwen3.5-9B. Two physicians rated the 400 de-identified responses by consensus for medical accuracy, completeness, safety, readability and reliability on a 0–1 scale, and responses with accuracy below 0.70 were classified as hallucinated. Hallucination rates were 2.5% for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 3.8% for TigerLLM-9B, 22.5% for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 77.5% for Qwen3.5-9B. Guideline grounding lowered the rate of Qwen3.5-9B to 11.3% (difference − 66.3 percentage points; 95% CI − 76.3 to − 55.0) and raised every criterion by 0.24 to 0.38 points (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). BanglaDiaRAG outscored Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on all five criteria and matched or exceeded TigerLLM-9B, but it remained below Gemma-4-26B-A4B in safety, readability and reliability, and its residual errors were specific, confident and potentially harmful. Guideline grounding can turn a weak general-purpose model into a much safer Bangla diabetes assistant, but the choice of base model mattered as much as retrieval and no configuration was free of hallucination, so clinical oversight remains essential before patient-facing use.

research.abstract: Abstract Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) can carry a protein family across deep phylogenetic divides, but whether a horizontally mobile family retains structural and functional integrity over such distances—and under what selective regime—remains poorly characterized in the Candidate Phyla Radiation (CPR), a radiation of streamlined, host-dependent genomes. Here we use the CPR-C4 cysteine protease family to address this question at genome-database scale. Across 6,411 CPR representative genomes, CPR-C4 homologs occur in only 14.0% of species and are entirely absent from Saccharimonadia (1,310 species), a patchy distribution incompatible with the family's previous description as "highly conserved" in CPR. Phylogenetic incongruence testing attributes this pattern to HGT: approximately unbiased tests reject the GTDB species tree (AU = 0.000; ΔLogL = 1,039), the Robinson–Foulds distance is 0.862, only 3/10 orders are monophyletic, and flanking regions are specifically enriched for conjugative transfer proteins (OR = 4.66, p = 8.6 × 10−8) but not for transposons or phages. Despite 27–62% pairwise sequence identity, 60 representative homologs spanning 7 classes and 30 orders all fold into high-confidence structures (mean pLDDT = 94.5), cross-validated by an architecturally independent language-model predictor, with 55/60 retaining the intact catalytic triad (Cys77–His109–Leu131). Structural contact conservation (71.5% in distant homologs) tracks sequence divergence (Spearman ρ = 0.69) while declining more slowly than sequence identity, and three independent tests reject hydrophobic core compensation. Instead, strong purifying selection (global dN/dS = 0.079), localized to the catalytic core by site-resolved analysis (FEL), maintains fold and catalytic geometry across transfers. Non-CPR homologs from the NCBI nr database are phylogenetically nested within CPR diversity, indicating a CPR-centered origin with repeated cross-phylum spillover, and carriage is sharply depleted in extreme environments (1/273 versus 786/4,698; phylogenetic bootstrap P = 0.0015) while remaining indifferent to host association. These results establish CPR-C4 as a horizontally mobile, functionally constrained protease family, show that strong purifying selection can preserve a catalytic fold across phylum-level transfers, and indicate that distribution claims for CPR gene families warrant re-examination at current genome scale.

research.abstract: Abstract Background. Clinical attachment loss (CAL) is widely used in population oral health research as an indicator of periodontal tissue destruction but can only be measured on teeth present at examination. Retained-dentition summaries may therefore underrepresent cumulative periodontal destruction when tooth loss is partly periodontal in origin. Objective. To develop and evaluate a framework for estimating periodontitis experience from cross-sectional data by incorporating informative tooth loss under etiological uncertainty. Methods. Data came from 10,324 dentate adults aged ≥30 years in NHANES 2009–2014 who completed periodontal and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) assessments. Expected Periodontitis Experience (EPE) combined observed CAL among retained teeth with the expected periodontal contribution of missing teeth. Published extraction-cause studies informed age-specific weights for missing teeth. EPE was compared with mean CAL and extent CAL ≥4 mm using survey-weighted age patterns and late-life curvature within glycemic groups. HbA1c was used as a theoretically related but distinct external measure. Results. Periodontal observability declined with age, particularly among adults with diabetes. Conventional observed-site measures showed weaker or declining fitted increases after age 70, whereas EPE retained a more consistently increasing age pattern. Late-life curvature was 0.06, 0.04, and −0.05 across glycemic groups for EPE, compared with −0.47, −0.91, and −2.70 for extent CAL ≥4 mm. EPE also showed the strongest rank correlation with HbA1c (ρ = 0.291 versus 0.238–0.255). Conclusions. Treating tooth loss as probabilistically informative may provide a more coherent representation of cumulative periodontal destruction in cross-sectional periodontal epidemiology, particularly at older ages.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT. Pulmonary melioidosis is frequently mistaken for pulmonary tuberculosis because of overlapping clinical and radiological features, often delaying appropriate treatment. We conducted a retrospective comparative cohort study at a tertiary care center in southern India between January 2018 and August 2025 to compare chest computed tomography (CT) features of microbiologically confirmed melioidosis and tuberculosis in diabetic adults who underwent CT within 30 days of symptom onset. A total of 151 patients were included: 46 with melioidosis and 105 with tuberculosis. Cavitation ( n = 81/105 [77.1%] versus n = 20/46 [43.5%], P <0.001) and hydropneumothorax ( n = 11/105 [10.5%] versus n = 0/46 [0%], P = 0.019) were more common in tuberculosis. In contrast, when compared with tuberculosis, melioidosis was associated with more frequent bilateral lung involvement ( n = 37/105 [35.2%] versus n = 26/46 [56.5%], P = 0.015), pleural effusion ( n = 28/105 [26.7%] versus n = 23/46 [50.0%], P = 0.005), and hilar lymphadenopathy ( n = 6/105 [5.7%] versus n = 8/46 [17.4%], P = 0.032). Despite these differences, there was substantial overlap in CT findings, with upper-lobe predominance, centrilobular nodules, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy seen in both groups. In multivariable analysis, cavitation was associated with significantly lower odds of melioidosis than tuberculosis (adjusted odds ratio: 0.25, 95% CI: 0.12–0.54, P <0.001). Pulmonary melioidosis and pulmonary tuberculosis, therefore, show substantial overlap on chest CT in diabetic patients, and imaging should be interpreted as an adjunct to targeted microbiological diagnosis rather than a substitute for it.

research.abstract: Abstract Pulmonary tuberculosis remains one of the most prevalent and threatening infectious diseases. Classical anti-tubercular therapy targets essential enzymes of the pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), thereby suppressing bacterial growth. However, the emergence of drug-resistant strains necessitates alternative therapeutic approaches. Virulence inhibition is a promising strategy that blocks Mtb virulence factors required for survival within host cells. We previously identified a hit compound, BTP15, which protected fibroblasts and THP-1 macrophages from Mtb-induced cell death ex vivo by blocking phagosomal escape through inhibition of the mycobacterial histidine kinase MprB. Due to poor pharmacokinetics, the structure of BTP15 was optimized. New benzothiophene derivatives were screened for MprB inhibition, microsomal stability, toxicity, and ex vivo efficacy in THP-1 and MRC-5 cells. The lead compound, 7a, exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic parameters, showed no toxicity in mice at 250 mg/kg, and prevented Mtb dissemination in an acute mouse model of tuberculosis.

research.abstract: Phylogenetic trees are hybrid objects: branch lengths vary continuously, while topologies change discretely through edge contractions and expansions. Billera-Holmes-Vogtmann (BHV) tree space provides a canonical geometry for this structure, representing each resolved topology as a Euclidean orthant and topological changes as motion across shared lower-dimensional boundaries. We introduce PhylaFlow, a hybrid flow-matching model that learns posterior-basin transport in BHV tree space. PhylaFlow is trained on BHV geodesic paths from random starting trees to short-run posterior samples, coupling continuous branch-length motion within orthants with learned boundary events and discrete topology transitions. We evaluate the learned geometry operationally: if the flow reaches posterior-relevant regions, finite-budget Bayesian refinement initialized from, or guided by, its terminal trees should recover posterior-supported topologies more efficiently. Across DS1-DS8 phylogenetic posterior benchmarks, PhylaFlow substantially reduces initial Tree-KL relative to classical initializers. After finite-budget MrBayes refinement, direct PhylaFlow improves early and intermediate topology-recovery trajectories on most datasets, while split-guided PhylaFlow-MCMC obtains the strongest hard-case results. The best PhylaFlow variant outperforms short-warmup on seven of eight datasets and PhyloGFN on five of eight under the same refinement budget. In a joint sequence-conditioned experiment, sequence embeddings steer posterior split recovery, although exact posterior topology recovery remains preliminary. These results show that hybrid flow matching can learn actionable transport in BHV tree space and provide a geometry-aware proposal mechanism for Bayesian phylogenetic inference.

research.abstract: Abstract The pathogenicity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis relies on its ability to withstand hostile host environments. Coenzyme F 420 is critical for redox metabolism in Mycobacterium tuberculosis , an organism distinguished by its abundant use of this low-redox-potential cofactor and a repertoire of F 420 -dependent enzymes. While F 420 -dependent mechanisms are known to confer protection against antimicrobials and oxidative stress, the specific enzymes responsible remain largely unidentified. In this study, using the F 420 -dependent detoxification of malachite green as a phenotypic marker, we performed a genome-wide screen in Mycobacterium tuberculosis using transposon mutagenesis and whole genome sequencing. The results of transposon mutagenesis and whole genome sequencing revealed that, among the 28 genes encoding F 420 -dependent enzymes, only mutations in fgd (essential for F 420 H 2 re-generation) and Rv2061c , a gene encoding a putative F 420 -dependent oxidoreductase, were highly susceptible to malachite green. Subsequent experiments confirmed that Rv2061c and its homolog MT2120 are required for detoxifying malachite green and crystal violet. Furthermore, the Rv2061c mutant exhibited increased susceptibility to isoniazid and pretomanid; as well as menadione-induced oxidative stress. We also identified mutations in the transcriptional repressor Rv0678 as a key determinant of resistance to malachite green and crystal violet. This study establishes Rv2061c as a pivotal F 420 -dependent oxidoreductase that protects Mycobacterium tuberculosis from malachite green and other antimicrobial compounds as well as oxidative stress and further supports Rv0678 as a master regulator of multidrug resistance. These findings expand our knowledge of Mycobacterium tuberculosis defense mechanisms and highlight F 420 -dependent pathways as a potential target for new drug development.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium abscessus (Mab) is a rapidly growing non-tuberculous mycobacterium that causes opportunistic infections and exhibits extensive intrinsic antibiotic resistance. The proline-glutamate (PE) and proline-proline-glutamate (PPE) protein families are mycobacteria-specific virulence factors implicated in immune modulation, antigenic variation, and persistence. While Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) harbors approximately 170 PE/PPE members, the repertoire of PE/PPE genes in Mab remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we performed a genome-wide survey of PE/PPE genes in Mab ATCC 19,977 and identified 18 candidate family members, representing a relatively small fraction of the genome compared with slow-growing mycobacteria. Most predicted proteins harbor canonical PE or PPE domains and display acidic physicochemical properties. Phylogenetic analysis resolved the proteins into three subfamilies: PE, PPE, and PE-PPE, revealing moderate structural diversity but limited family expansion. Motif and gene structure analyses supported the evolutionary conservation. Notably, no PE_polymorphic GC-rich repetitive sequence (PE_PGRS) or PPE_major polymorphic tandem repeat (PPE_MPTR) members were detected, suggesting lineage-specific genomic reduction relative to other pathogenic mycobacteria. AlphaFold predictions revealed conserved N-terminal folds and variable C-terminal regions, which may contribute to functional diversification. Subcellular localization predictions indicated that most proteins are extracellular. Synteny analysis revealed no detectable collinearity among these genes. Transcriptomic analyses revealed condition-dependent expression of PE/PPE genes during amoeba and macrophage infection and under artificial sputum medium and metal ion stress, suggesting roles in environmental adaptation and host interaction. This study provides the first systematic overview of PE/PPE gene repertoire in Mab and lays the groundwork for elucidating their roles in intracellular survival, host interaction, and antimicrobial resistance.

research.abstract: Introduction. Mycobacterium tuberculosis has held an exceptional presence in medical research, especially in recent years (1). While pulmonary infections largely remain the focus of literature and public health initiatives (2), extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) infections have been gaining prominence due to their increasing prevalence, particularly in populations characterized by a low incidence of tuberculosis (2–4). Although EPTB infections, such as tuberculous meningitis, carry a high mortality risk (5), delays in diagnosis and treatment persist. These delays are driven by their diverse, non-specific clinical presentations, coupled with the variable performance of diagnostic modalities like the Cartridge-Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (CBNAAT) (6–10). While general literature regarding the use and efficacy of CBNAAT in diagnosing EPTB exists (2,11–15), studies focusing on its sensitivity and specificity in paucibacillary specimens are an evolving niche (16). Since there is a greater prevalence of paucibacillary EPTB specimens in our setting, where such an analysis has not been conducted, we performed a retrospective study to understand the overarching diagnostic performance of our existing modalities in EPTB specimens. Methods. An observational retrospective study was conducted with the data collected between 2019 and 2022 at a tertiary care centre in central Kerala, India. A total of 105 specimens – categorized as pleural, lymph node, pus, tissue, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), peritoneal and others – from presumptive EPTB cases were included in the study. The samples underwent acid-fast bacilli staining microscopy, liquid culture and CBNAAT utilizing the GeneXpert platform. The results were recorded, and the data were analysed with P< 0.05 considered statistically significant. Observations and Results. In the 105 samples collected for the study, 6 (5.7%) were positive on Ziehl–Nielsen staining, 26 (24.8%) samples grew M. tuberculosis complex on liquid culture and CBNAAT detected M. tuberculosis in 16 (15.2%) specimens. The sensitivity and specificity of CBNAAT, with culture as the gold standard, were found to be 50.0 and 96.2%, respectively. The sensitivity and specificity of CBNAAT for pus, peritoneal (including tissue and fluid aspirate), pleural fluids, CSF, lymph nodes and other miscellaneous sample types ranged from 33.3 to 100% and 85.7 to 100%, respectively. Among smear-negative specimens, the sensitivity and specificity of CBNAAT were 42.9 and 96.2%, respectively, whereas in smear-positive specimens, the sensitivity increased to 80.0%. Conclusion. CBNAAT is a viable tool for the detection of M. tuberculosis ; however, in paucibacillary specimens, its use along with other methods like smear and culture could lead to better identification of the mycobacteria.

research.abstract: Abstract Hybridization is increasingly recognized as a widespread evolutionary process across animals, plants, and fungi, and plays a key role in driving speciation, shaping genetic diversity, and facilitating adaptation. Initial hybrid genomes are rarely observed empirically, making it challenging to observe in real time how competing forces like purifying selection and adaptive introgression interact to shape post-hybridization genomes. Here, we use replicated experimental hybrid populations between Drosophila simulans and D. sechellia to track directly genome-wide evolutionary dynamics across approximately 45 generations post-hybridization. We show that hybrid populations with primarily D. simulans ancestry rapidly recover wild-type levels of fertility and fecundity, whereas populations carrying predominantly D. sechellia ancestry experience persistent fitness reductions and frequent extinction. Genome-wide ancestry trajectories show pervasive purifying selection against minority-ancestry alleles, leading to rapid regression toward majority ancestry across the genome, with stronger purging on the X chromosome than autosomes. Following the initial purging, neutral minority ancestry stabilized at low frequencies across the genome. In striking contrast, we observe repeated increases in D. sechellia ancestry on chromosome 4 and multiple regions on chromosome 3R within D. simulans -majority populations, providing evidence for adaptive introgression. High-density sequencing revealed that these regions were repeatedly retained across independently evolving populations despite near-complete genome-wide purging. Simulations support a model in which recombination rapidly uncouples beneficial introgressed alleles from linked incompatibility-associated alleles during the initial generations, allowing positive selection to act. Our temporal allele-frequency analyses suggest that hybrid genome stabilization of the introgressed regions is highly repeatable but not identical, yielding parallel outcomes across replicate populations. We establish a tractable experimental framework to directly observe how hybrid genomes reorganize in real time, and demonstrate how purifying selection, positive selection, recombination, and stochastic processes interact to restructure hybrid genomes shortly after admixture.

research.abstract: Abstract Background In three national surveys, no cross-national ranking of diet-attributable metabolic burden was identified: the apparent ordering moved with the definition of the outcome and with the validity of the dietary index. Both were tested. Subjects/Methods We harmonised individual-participant data from national surveys in the USA (NHANES 2017–2018), Korea (KNHANES 2015–2021) and Mexico (ENSANUT 2018–2019); 56,365 adults in total, recovered Mexican blood-pressure data from the raw files, and defined metabolic syndrome (MetS) with a common five-component ATP III rule. We estimated survey-weighted sex-specific associations of the energy-adjusted Dietary Inflammatory Index (E-DII) with MetS, country-specific population-attributable fractions (PAFs) on a common counterfactual scale, and the E-DII’s correlation with log high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP). A quantitative bias analysis examined whether validity differences could reverse the country ordering. Results The E-DII–MetS association was larger in women (USA OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.98–1.55; Korea 1.078, 1.028–1.132; Mexico 1.074, 0.992–1.163; interaction P=0.080) but disappeared without blood pressure in the outcome (pooled 1.065, 0.982–1.155; P=0.13). Female PAFs were 15.0%, 7.6% and 3.8%; no pairwise difference was distinguishable (all P≥0.23). E-DII validity was 0.137 in US women versus 0.040 in Korean women (P=2.0×10−4); the validity ratio was 0.29, correction reversed the observed ordering, and its interval straddled the reversal threshold. Conclusions Neither the direction nor the magnitude of cross-national differences in diet-attributable MetS burden was identified; the ordering was bounded by outcome definition and by index validity. Cross-national burden comparisons require local validation of both.

research.abstract: Objectives: To assess whether local artificial intelligence updates for diabetic retinopathy screening that improve image-level probabilities also improve patient-level detection, flagging and net benefit. Methods: This retrospective evaluation used four systems, BRSET source data and two external cohorts, mBRSET and DeepDRiD, with separate audit and evaluation patients. Updates were fitted and selected on audits of 25-200 patients; probability recalibration and operating policies were selected separately. Outcomes included Brier loss, patient detection, flags and net benefit at four threshold probabilities (p=0.05-0.30). Comparators were no update, flag all and flag none. Conditional patient-cluster intervals compared updates with no update; simple-policy comparisons were descriptive. Results: At audit budget 200, mean Brier loss improved in all eight cohort-system comparisons. In mBRSET, flags rose from 154-442 to 809-951 per 1,000 patients and missed positives fell from 51-133 to 2-14 (5.69-9.48 additional flags per additional detection). In mBRSET at p=0.05, three of four updates had lower mean net benefit than flag all; at p=0.20, all four exceeded flag all but remained below no update. In DeepDRiD at p=0.20, the APTOS update increased mean net benefit by 0.0510 over no update and exceeded both simple policies. Discussion: Image-level improvement did not ensure patient-level benefit. Flag increases were consistent with image-level targets applied to patients with about four images. Conclusion: Local updates should be judged on patient-level detection, flags and net benefit against unchanged, flag-all and flag-none policies, not on image-level metrics alone.

research.abstract: Long COVID (LC) affects millions of individuals worldwide, particularly those with preexisting comorbidities. However, when assessing comorbidity-related risk factors for LC, it remains unclear whether preexisting comorbidities should be defined prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection or LC diagnosis. This methodological choice may substantially bias estimates of LC risk. In this study, leveraging Electronic Health Records (EHR) from 6,130,413 adults with documented COVID-19 across 49 U.S. states in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C) from 2020 to 2024, we evaluated the impact of different comorbidity exposure-window definitions on LC risk estimates. We developed ensemble cross-fitted double/debiased machine learning to adjust for individual- and county- level confounders. We found that defining comorbidities before infection rather than before LC diagnosis yielded 8%-314% higher adjusted attributable risks and 3%-34% higher adjusted relative risks across 16 major comorbidities. Comorbidity-associated risks generally declined from 2020 to 2024, while substantial demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and multimorbidity-related disparities persisted. Exposure-window specification can be a major source of bias in estimates of LC risk, particularly for comorbidities prone to delayed clinical recognition or underascertainment. More broadly, our results highlight how temporal misclassification of exposures in longitudinal EHR studies can distort risk attribution and population-level inference for risk stratification for LC and prioritization of prevention strategies in clinical medicine and public health, respectively.

research.abstract: Abstract Background/Objectives Chronic wounds such as diabetic foot ulcers, venous leg ulcers and burns are a major health-care burden. Extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) is a non-invasive treatment that promotes angiogenesis and tissue regeneration. This review synthesizes the clinical evidence for ESWT in wound management, and asks how contemporary reviews reflect it. Methods PubMed and Ovid/Embase were searched from inception to 1 September 2026 according to PRISMA, regardless of wound type, study design or ESWT modality. Fifty-one clinical studies and 46 prior reviews were analyzed. Heterogeneity confined the primary synthesis to a qualitative one; an exploratory pooled analysis was performed for the one endpoint reported consistently enough to permit it. Results None of the 46 previously published reviews covered the original evidence in its full breadth: each cited a median of 19.4% of the clinical studies available at its reference date (range 0-90.9%), and systematic reviews covered no more than narrative ones. Most studies reported improved healing across all four modalities. In seven controlled trials reporting complete healing as events and denominators, the pooled risk ratio favored ESWT (1.51, 95% CI 1.22-1.87; I 2 = 0%; 689 patients). Such data existed for three modalities only, resting on one trial for two, so modalities could not be compared. Conclusions ESWT is a useful adjunct for acute and chronic wounds. Because no previous review reflected the evidence base as a whole, conclusions drawn from it should be read with caution. Head-to-head trials with matched physical dose are needed before any modality can be preferred.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lineage 8 (L8) occupies a unique phylogenetic position as a sister clade to all other known Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) lineages. Although the initial identification of L8 strains was limited to Rwanda and Uganda, the complete geographical distribution of this lineage remains undetermined due to limited genomic surveillance across eastern and central Africa. METHODS: We performed whole genome sequencing (WGS) on MTBC isolates from rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (TB) patients' sputum in Bukavu, South Kivu province, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Lineage assignment was performed using TBProfiler with classification based on single nucleotide polymporphisms (SNPs). Phylogenetic reconstruction was conducted using maximum likelihood analysis against publicly available L8 reference genomes from Rwanda and Uganda. Drug-resistance profiles were determined through both genotypic prediction from WGS data and phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing. Clinical and epidemiologic data were extracted from programmatic records. RESULTS: We identified three clinical isolates belonging to MTBC L8 among fifteen sequenced isolates collected in Bukavu between January and December 2023 enriched for rifampicin resistant TB as determined by Xpert Ultra. Ancestral genomic features characteristic of L8 were preserved, including the intact cobF region and complete pks8 gene. Drug-resistance prediction from genomic data indicated multidrug-resistant and pre-extensively-resistant TB. Systematic genomic surveillance across the DRC-Uganda-Rwanda-Burundi corridor, including rifampicin-susceptible isolates, is needed to determine whether L8 represents a rare relict lineage or an under-detected endemic variant circulating through regional transmission networks.

research.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global public health concern, with Gram-negative carbapenem-resistant bacteria (CRG) classified by WHO as critical priority pathogens. Biomedical waste disposal sites (BMWs) may act as reservoirs for resistant organisms, posing occupational and community risks. This study investigated the phenotypic and genotypic characterization of Gram-negative carbapenem-resistant bacteria in bioaerosols collected from BMW facilities in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. Bioaerosols were sampled using active Six-stage Andersen Impactors and passive settled plates. Isolates were identified by MALDI-TOF, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST). Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was performed for 26 representative isolates, and resistance gene profiling was conducted using CARD and ResFinder databases. Representative isolates belonged to Moraxellaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, and Pseudomonadaceae families. All species showed resistance to linezolid, and approximately 60% were multidrug resistant to carbapenems, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones. Genotypic analysis confirmed the prevalence of carbapenemase genes, with blaNDM-1 most frequent, followed by blaNDM-7, blaVIM-2, blaVIM-11, blaOXA-23, and blaOXA-235. This is the first report documenting Acinetobacter baumannii, A. schindleri, A. towneri, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas juntendi in bioaerosols from BMW sites. Biomedical waste environments serve as critical reservoirs of AMR. These findings emphasize the need for surveillance, protective measures, and integration of environmental AMR monitoring into public health policy.

research.abstract: Background. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) involves progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction, but conserved islet programs require cross-cohort and single-cell validation. Methods. We integrated four human islet transcriptomic cohorts using differential expression, random-effects meta-analysis, Hallmark scoring, and module scoring. To test generalizability without reusing held-out outcomes, modules were re-derived from three cohorts and scored in the fourth in rotating study-level cross-fitting, with expression- and detection-matched random gene-set nulls. Machine-learning performance in GSE164416 was estimated by nested stratified 5-fold cross-validation with DEG calling and feature selection repeated within each outer training fold. An annotation-compatible score was tested in GSE50244, and beta-cell validation used GSE221156. Results. Cross-fitted IsletDysfunctionScore effects were positive in all four held-out cohorts (d = 0.39-1.36; pooled Hedges g = 0.905, 95% CI 0.501-1.309, p = 1.14 x 10^-5, I2 = 5.5%). Matched gene-set null testing supported effects beyond random expectation in two cohorts. Nested machine learning yielded AUC = 0.960 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.900-0.997); GABRA2 and ENSG00000284653 were selected in all outer folds. The external 8-gene consensus-pool score achieved AUC = 0.907 (DeLong 95% CI 0.818-0.996), but its fixed threshold did not transfer. In GSE221156, the single-cell dysfunction-score analog increased and BetaIdentitySecretion decreased in T2D; ImmuneStress was nominally increased but did not survive false-discovery correction across the single-cell score family. Conclusions. Human T2D islets show a reproducible stress/identity-loss framework that generalizes directionally under study-level cross-fitting and beta-cell-resolved validation. The candidate panel is a research transcriptomic signature requiring further validation.

research.abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) have improved substantially in predictive performance, yet results remain difficult to compare across studies that differ in cohorts, phenotype definitions, and evaluation procedures. Comparison to machine-learning methods is harder still, since their performance depends strongly on how data are partitioned and whether related individuals leak across splits. Here, we introduce a family-aware benchmark for polygenic prediction built on version 9 of the All of Us Research Program (AoU). The benchmark assigns entire family components to fixed discovery, calibration, and test partitions, reserves first-degree relatives for within-family evaluation, and separates models trained only on AoU discovery data from those using external GWAS summary statistics. This enables direct comparison between conventional PRS pipelines and machine-learning models trained under identical data budgets. We report results for 14 binary disease traits. Our strongest scores explain 5.7-24.9% of liability-scale variance, with particularly strong prediction for Alzheimer's disease, type 2 diabetes, prostate cancer, glaucoma, and inflammatory bowel disease, and match or exceed published commercial and academic scores for most traits. Across 12 traits with interpretable within-family estimates of within-sibship-to-population effect ratio, 11 confidence intervals included a ratio of 1. Type 2 diabetes showed an attenuation ratio of 0.86 [0.76, 0.97].

research.abstract: Wearable accelerometers enable continuous monitoring of physical activity (PA), yet conventional summary measures and population-wide clustering approaches may overlook disease-associated behavioral heterogeneity. Here we introduce LocPA, a computational framework that identifies disease-enriched PA patterns through confounder-adjusted activity profiling, similarity network construction, local disease-enrichment testing and community detection. Applying LocPA to 24-hour accelerometry profiles from the UK Biobank, we identified two recurring PA phenotypes across six diseases spanning cardiometabolic, neurological, psychiatric, renal and cardiovascular conditions: a low-activity phenotype characterized by reduced daytime activity and a sleep-disrupted phenotype characterized by reduced daytime and elevated nocturnal activity. In hypertension and diabetes, the sleep-disrupted phenotype was associated with greater disease burden and less favorable clinical and metabolic profiles, differences not consistently captured by conventional PA summary measures. LocPA also identified disease-specific temporal patterns, particularly in Parkinsons disease. Analyses in an independent National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort supported the recurrence of hypertension- and diabetes-enriched patterns across populations and accelerometry measurements. LocPA provides a flexible, disease-driven approach for uncovering clinically relevant temporal PA patterns, with potential applications in disease risk characterization and personalized behavioral interventions.

research.abstract: Background The 2026 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome guideline broadens recommendations for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), but the increment over pre-2026 standards is unknown. We estimated the number and clinical profile of US adults newly eligible under this guideline. Methods Cross-sectional analysis of adults aged 30-79 years in the 2011-2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Adults were newly eligible if they met 2026 CKM guideline indications but not pre-2026 American Diabetes Association, American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association heart failure, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes, or obesity guideline indications. Sensitivity analyses used 2 US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) label standards. Results Among 175.17 million US adults, 111.84 million (63.8%) were already eligible for either class. The CKM guideline added 7.48 million (95% CI: 6.48 to 8.47), a 6.7% increase, all for GLP-1RA and none for SGLT2i: 6.49 million with overweight (body mass index 27.0-29.9 kg/m2, ethnicity adjusted) and no other cardiometabolic disease, and 0.99 million with type 2 diabetes and 10-year PREVENT cardiovascular risk ?7.5%. Newly eligible adults (86.8% CKM stage 1) were younger (46.2 vs 52.9 years), leaner (27.8 vs 33.0 kg/m2), and at lower 10- and 30-year PREVENT risk (3.6% vs 8.1%; 11.3% vs 19.6%; all P < 0.001). Against FDA labeling, 14.15-25.17 million were newly eligible (7.66-18.20 million for SGLT2i). Assuming a 20% relative risk reduction, the projected number needed to treat per cardiovascular event prevented was 243 over 10 years and 56 over 30 years (ages 30-59) in adults with overweight, versus 61 and 26 in already eligible adults. Conclusions Relative to pre-2026 society guidelines, the 2026 CKM guideline newly confers a GLP-1RA indication on 7.48 million US adults, predominantly at lower cardiovascular risk. Whether treating these adults improves outcomes in a cost-efficient manner remains to be established.

research.abstract: Introduction Large language models (LLMs) may enable the extraction of clinically relevant information from unstructured electronic health records, but most previous work focused on identifying diagnoses without preserving their temporal context. We evaluated the ability of an LLM to extract diagnoses and associated dates from longitudinal clinical reports. Methods In an observational study using the Bern Sleep-Wake Registry, diagnostic annotations from 248 patients comprising 2343 clinical entries were analyzed. Six common comorbidity groups, subdivided into 32 hierarchical diagnostic categories, were evaluated. Using gpt-oss-20b, we extracted diagnosis presence, the number of diagnostic instances, and dates per instance. A reference standard was established through independent review by two physicians, with disagreements adjudicated by a third physician. LLM performance was assessed using diagnostic classification and temporal agreement. Direct annotation costs were compared. Results At the patient level, the LLM achieved an overall F1 score of 0.88 for diagnosis presence and 0.96 for the presence of a reported date. For the earliest reported diagnosis date, agreement with the reference standard was 86.73% at the day level. When considering the cumulative set of dates for each diagnosis, date recall was 87.63%, the extra-date rate was 20.88%, and full agreement was achieved in 58.19% of cases. Human annotators showed substantial disagreement in temporal annotation, with a date recall of 75.49%, an extra-date rate of 17.89%, and full agreement in 58.64% of cases. LLM-based extraction reduced direct annotation costs by 94.65%. Conclusions LLMs can extract diagnoses and their dates from heterogeneous clinical text with high agreement with an adjudicated reference standard. These findings support the scalable use of LLMs for longitudinal clinical registries.

research.abstract: Abstract Salticidae (jumping spiders) is the most species‐rich family within Araneae. Despite recent advances in phylogenomic studies, mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) evolution and its contribution to understanding phylogenetic relationships in Salticidae remain poorly characterized. Here, we present a mitochondrial phylogenomic analysis of 107 salticid species representing all seven recognized subfamilies. Using newly generated and publicly available mitogenomes, we investigated phylogenetic relationships and evolutionary patterns across the family, with a particular focus on comparisons between the highly diverse Salticinae and the species‐poor non‐Salticinae lineages. Our results show that the salticid mitogenomes are highly conserved in overall structure, with broadly similar genome size and nucleotide composition between Salticinae and non‐Salticinae lineages. Codon usage showed a pronounced A/T bias, with both mutational pressure and natural selection contributing to codon usage patterns. Phylogenetic analyses strongly supported the monophyly of Salticidae and all seven subfamilies in the maximum likelihood and Bayesian analyses. Lyssomaninae and Asemoneinae were recovered as sister groups, as were Eupoinae and Spartaeinae, while Onomastinae was sister to the clade comprising Hisponinae and Salticinae. Within Salticinae, Amycoida and Salticoida were recovered as major lineages, although relationships within Salticoida were unstable among analytical methods. Selection analyses indicated that all 13 mitochondrial protein‐coding genes are predominantly under purifying selection, whereas nad2 showed the most consistent signals of positive selection in Salticinae across the branch‐site, FEL and MEME analyses. Fifteen distinct gene rearrangement patterns were identified in Salticidae, including 13 novel patterns, with M5 inferred as the gene order of the most recent common ancestor of Salticidae. Gene rearrangements were more diverse in non‐Salticinae, particularly within Spartaeinae. Transposition was inferred as the predominant type of mitochondrial gene rearrangements in Salticidae. Overall, this study provides mitochondrial evidence for phylogenetic relationships within Salticidae and contributes to our understanding of mitochondrial sequence evolution, selection and gene order evolution in jumping spiders.

research.abstract: PurposeThis study aimed to identify the demographic and clinical predictors of statin adherence among patients prescribed statins for the primary prevention of CVD during the first two years following their first recorded statin prescription, using real-world data. MethodsThe Electronic Practice Based Research Network Linked Dataset was used in this study. Statin adherence was calculated using a modified proportion of days covered (PDC), based on prescribing data from the date of the first recorded statin prescription to the to the last recorded visit within the two years observation period. Patients with a PDC [≥] 80% were classified as adherent. All analyses were performed using R software. Descriptive analyses and multivariate logistic regression were performed. Backward stepwise selection guided by the Akaike Information Criterion was used to derive a parsimonious final model. ResultsOverall, 3,432 patients accounting for 57,227 visits were included. The mean PDC was 91.6% ({+/-}22.2%), and 72.0% of patients were classified as adherent. Higher odds of adherence was observed among patients aged over 65 years (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 1.4, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.1 - 1.8), those residing in Socio-Economic Indexes for Australia 2021 Index of Relative Socio-Economic Advantage and Disadvantage category 3 (AOR 2.1, 95% CI 1.6 - 2.9), those prescribed three medications, including a statin (AOR 1.8, 95% CI 1.3 - 2.4) and those with one selected comorbidity (AOR 1.4, 95% CI 1.1 - 1.7), compared with their respective reference categories. Patients prescribed two or more statin types had lower odds of adherence (AOR 0.7, 95% CI 0.5 - 0.9). ConclusionsAge, area level socioeconomic status, and the number of prescribed medications, selected comorbidities and statin types were associated with statin adherence. However, adherence was estimated from prescribing rather than dispensing data, and the model demonstrated modest discrimination. Further validation in independent populations is needed to validate these associations.

research.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) transmission is sustained in part by asymptomatic disease states that limit the effectiveness of passive case finding interventions that rely on symptom-based diagnosis. Transmission models commonly represent the time spent with aTB using a single disease state, thereby imposing an exponentially distributed waiting time and a constant hazard of leaving that state. We evaluated how differences in the shape of the aTB waiting-time distribution affect the fit to observed disease progression data and subsequent projections of TB incidence and active case finding (ACF) impact. We fitted exponential and chained-state gamma formulations to cohort data on aTB progression and incorporated them into transmission models. The gamma-distributed model fits the data at least as well the exponential model indicating that the alternative model structures can also capture the changes of aTB cases. Comparing the fitted gamma-distributed model and the exponential model, we quantify how assumptions about the distribution of the duration of asymptomatic TB affect future disease trajectories and the expected impact of ACF interventions. Using India as a case study, we found that the gamma-distributed model projects a slower decline in TB incidence under the status quo, but a substantially larger reduction in the projected incidence of TB when ACF is employed, compared with the exponential model. These results suggest that estimates of ACF impact, and consequently assessments of its cost-effectiveness, may be sensitive to assumptions regarding the shape of waiting-time distribution of asymptomatic disease, indicating the importance of a better understanding of the natural history of asymptomatic disease for projecting of intervention effects.

research.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is one of the fastest-growing epidemics associated with cognitive impairment and dementia. This reduces quality of life among patients with diabetes. Several trials on the management of cognitive impairment have been conducted, although their effectiveness and mechanisms are still unclear. Aim: To synthesize evidence from systematic reviews and meta-analyses of RCTs examining interventions for cognitive impairment in T2DM, stratified by intervention category, comparator, patient characteristics, mechanisms, and clinical outcomes. Methods: We identified 11 systematic reviews (n = 213,604 participants) reporting the effects of cognitive impairment interventions through a comprehensive literature search. Using random-effects models, a meta-meta-analysis was conducted and heterogeneity assessed using I{superscript 2} statistics. AMSTAR and GRADE were used to assess the quality of reviews. Subgroup analyses were conducted for intervention category, cognitive severity, age, diabetes duration, sex, and follow-up duration. Results: Sodium glucose co-transporter inhibitors showed the strongest cognitive improvement effect (pooled OR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.35-0.55; SUCRA = 94.5%), followed by GLP-1 receptor agonists (RR/OR = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.50-0.72; SUCRA = 92.1%). Among lifestyle interventions, multi-component exercise was the most effective (SMD = 0.69-1.04). The lower baseline cognition (MMSE < 23) benefited more from GLP-1 receptor agonists (Cohen's d = -3.00, p < 0.001). Advanced age ([≥]60 years) and prolonged intervention time ([≥]24 weeks for medications; [≥]6 months for exercise) were associated with greater effects. Female gender showed greater benefit from GLP-1 receptor agonists (HR = 0.63 vs 0.81 for male gender). Conclusions: SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists have the greatest effect on cognition in T2DM, and multi-component exercise is the most effective lifestyle component. The review therefore recommends individualized selection of interventions based on patient characteristics and baseline cognitive status. This calls for high-quality trials with prolonged follow-up to strengthen the evidence base.

research.abstract: We asked what topological structure adds to a clinical prediction model and how that addition should be measured. Drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) treatment outcome prediction is the testbed. The contribution is an evaluation design and a bounded null result. Cross-sectional records for 9210 patients from the NIAID TB Portals programme were collated to one row per patient by worst-case aggregation, giving a 99-feature clinical schema. We derived two topological representations. A Mapper graph, built on a UMAP lens over a Gower dissimilarity, supplied four neighbourhood-position features. Local Vietoris--Rips persistent homology on each patient's 26-point neighbourhood supplied degree-0 and degree-1 summaries, vectorised by the best of thirteen catalogued methods. We compared five feature configurations across four classifiers in a pipeline in which every topological step is fitted inside the training partition. A sealed test lockbox of 1776 patients, 463 of them with adverse outcomes, was opened once. We compared discrimination by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) using paired DeLong tests with Bonferroni correction (corrected threshold 0.0125). No topologically augmented configuration meaningfully improved lockbox AUROC over the clinical-only baseline under any classifier. The best AUROC was 0.7548, achieved by the baseline with XGBoost. Across all sixteen comparisons the upper 95% confidence limit never exceeded +0.014 AUROC. Five comparisons met the corrected threshold. Four favoured the baseline, and one, under the support vector machine, favoured the augmented model by a negligible +0.0005 AUROC.The same features supported neighbourhood-based risk stratification and revealed variation in adverse-outcome composition across patient neighbourhoods: adverse-outcome purity ranged from 5.9% to 30.5% across the fifteen largest Mapper nodes, stably under resampling. The findings support a complementary framing of topological data analysis in clinical prediction. Topological features are best understood not as replacements for clinical predictors but as an analytical lens that reveals geometric structure in the patient population not captured by the clinical feature representation alone.
